task: p50w2-arb7250-n03-dense-dem-cfd · dense particle-fluid coupling closure anchors: Richardson-Zaki expansion / Ergun pressure drop / minimum fluidisation + added mass and pressure-gradient force

decision.question: Does the assembled unresolved (point-particle) force closure -- Schiller-Naumann, Wen-Yu voidage correction, Di Felice, Ergun/Gidaspow dense branch, explicit pressure-gradient force and Maxey-Riley added mass, all switchable -- reproduce the three classical dense-bed anchors (Richardson-Zaki expansion index, Ergun pressure drop at both ends of the Re range, minimum fluidisation velocity), converge under grid refinement, conserve mass/momentum/energy, and fail in the three pre-declared negative controls?

alternatives.A_chosen: Periodic homogeneous bed element: N representative spheres in a 1-D column, quasi-steady fluid momentum balance, particle equation of motion integrated with RK4 including added mass on the effective mass. Anchors obtained by *dynamic* inversion (integrate the coupled ODE to its fixed point, bisect on u_s), not by algebraic rearrangement.
alternatives.B_rejected: Free-surface 1-D two-fluid column with contact stress (run in attempt 1 exploratory prototyping): the homogeneous anchors are then contaminated by free-surface smearing and solid-pressure stiffness, the vertical-grid error is first order (delta-x halving ratio ~2, below the pre-declared 2.5), and the steady voidage acquires an O(dx/H) surface bias that propagates into the log-slope n. Kept only as the mass-conserving expansion identity H/H0 = phi0/phi.
alternatives.C_rejected: Algebraic closure inversion only (no dynamics): it cannot distinguish an implementation bug in the coupled force assembly from a closure property, and it makes criteria 1/6 vacuous.

hypothesis.H1_momentum: With a normalised hat-kernel deposition the particle->fluid reaction is the exact negative of the particle force, so |sum F_f->p + sum F_p->f| / sum|F| is at machine precision (<= 1e-12) at eps_s = 0.3 and 0.5.
hypothesis.H2_richardson_zaki: For fine sand in water (d = 100 um, Re_t = 0.73, the regime where the RZ correlation was established) the Wen-Yu-corrected closure implies a voidage exponent n that matches the tabulated RZ correlation to <= 5%, and eps(u_s) is monotone.
hypothesis.H3_ergun: The discrete fluid momentum balance across a static bed reproduces rho_f g H + the classic Ergun porous-media drop to <= 5% at one viscous-dominated and one inertial-dominated velocity.
hypothesis.H4_umf: The dynamically inverted minimum fluidisation velocity agrees with the closed-form Ergun quadratic to <= 8%, and the drift velocity changes sign across it (settling below, entrainment above).
hypothesis.H5_grid: The pressure drop of a graded bed, with the voidage the CFD grid actually sees (hat filter of half width 2 dx), converges at second order, so halving dx reduces the error by >= 2.5.
hypothesis.H6_conservation: Solid mass in the conservative flux form, the inter-phase power pair and the discrete energy-ledger identity close to <= 1e-10.
hypothesis.H7_negative_controls: NC1 (no particle->fluid reaction) changes the bed pressure drop by > 20%; NC2 (drag coefficient x2, Newton regime) moves the terminal velocity by 2**-0.5 within 2%; NC3 (no pressure-gradient force) breaks the submerged-weight balance by > 20%.

outcome_metrics.momentum_residual: |sum F_p + sum R_cell| / sum|F|, worst over eps_s in {0.3, 0.5}, plus the drag-density-vs-pressure-drop cross-check
outcome_metrics.rz_index: log-log least-squares slope of u_s(eps) over eps in [0.55, 0.95] (9 points), dynamic route; deviation from n(Re_t) of the tabulated correlation
outcome_metrics.ergun_error: relative difference between the measured and the analytic pressure drop, uniform and graded bed, at u = 0.01 (inertial fraction 4.5%) and u = 0.30 (58%)
outcome_metrics.umf_error: relative difference between the dynamic root and the Ergun quadratic, plus the sign of the drift velocity at 0.9 u_mf and 1.15 u_mf
outcome_metrics.grid_error_ratio: successive error ratios of the graded-bed pressure drop for dx halving, 5 levels (20..320 cells)
outcome_metrics.conservation: mass drift (flux form), inter-phase power-pair residual, discrete ledger identity residual, quadrature-limited mechanical closure with its dt-convergence ratio

baseline_and_controls.analytic_references: Ergun (1952) porous-media quadratic; Richardson & Zaki (1954) tabulated exponent; single-sphere Schiller-Naumann and Newton drag; textbook u_mf quadratic root
baseline_and_controls.independent_route: every anchor is computed twice: dynamically (coupled ODE) and algebraically (closure inversion); the two must agree (reported as dynamic_vs_algebraic_relative)

negative_controls.NC1: fluid_reaction = False: the fluid momentum balance loses the drag source, so the bed pressure drop reverts to hydrostatic
negative_controls.NC2: cd_scale = 2 in the Newton regime (constant C_D, Re > 1000): terminal velocity must scale as 2**-0.5. The Stokes-regime cross-check (Re-dependent C_D) is reported and is explicitly *not* 2**-0.5
negative_controls.NC3: pressure_gradient = False: the Model-A balance loses the buoyancy channel and u_mf must move by > 20%

baseline_and_controls.internal_teeth: the momentum audit is re-run with the reaction disabled (must fail at O(1)); the mass advection test is re-run in non-conservative (advective) form (must drift at the percent level)

sweep_design.rationale: one operating point per anchor in the closure's validity window; closure sensitivity is reported as a table (wen_yu, di_felice, gidaspow, schiller_naumann) instead of being tuned away

variables_and_confounders.controlled: temperature-independent fluid properties held at the stated values; particle count and cell count fixed per case; identical integrator and closure assembly across anchors
variables_and_confounders.varied: voidage (RZ sweep), superficial velocity (Ergun), grid spacing (criterion 5), time step (ledger), closure switches (sensitivity table)

confounders.closure_vs_implementation: an anchor can pass because closure and reference share an algebraic form; mitigated by the dynamic route and by reporting cross-closure sensitivity
confounders.closure_validity_window: the RZ correlation is only meaningful at low Re_t; the study declares d = 100 um (Re_t = 0.73) as the anchor case and reports the higher-Re deviations as out-of-window
confounders.quadrature_in_the_energy_ledger: the mechanical closure is trapezoid-limited; the 1e-10 threshold is applied to the algebraic identities only and the quadrature-limited closure is reported with its own convergence ratio
confounders.free_surface_absence: no contacts and no free surface in the bed element; the effect on n is not measured here (declared limitation)

environment.repo_commit: recorded in the study JSON environment block at run time

analysis_plan: All criteria are computed from the code paths that the test-suite exercises; the JSON is written by the benchmark (no transcription). A criterion passes only if its measured value satisfies the predeclared threshold; an honest FAIL is reported verbatim if a threshold is missed. No threshold was changed after inspecting results.
interpretation_limits: homogeneous bed element: no particle contacts, no free surface, no fluid inertia or turbulence at the particle scale

the fluid is quasi-steady: the interstitial Reynolds number (Re_superficial up to 60) is far below the range where fluid inertia matters for the interphase force, but this is an assumption, not a measurement
monodisperse spheres only; polydispersity is a separate closure question
the grid criterion measures the resolution of the voidage field (the unresolved-coupling 'grid'); it is not a wall-normal resolution study of a resolved simulation
